newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Nov 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Nov 13.

text.p: CSX Corp and Conrail Inc are expected to reaffirm an $8.5 billion merger accord after they were unable to agree on a new CSX offer, the Wall Street Journal reported.
Other top stories included:
- Interval Research plans to spin off three start-up companies.
- Sunbeam Corp will cut half of its 12,000-strong workforce and sell or consolidate 39 of its 53 facilities.
- Major airlines are trying to block new carriers from making a presence at large airports, according to a government study.
- Agriculture oficials boosted their estimates for U.S. Midwest harvests.
- Smith Barney's legal strategy might have contributed to the negative publicity it had received over a lawsuit.
- A group of advertizing executives wants to get the industry to consider a voluntary curb on tobacco commercials to keep them from attracting children.
- Boeing Co, TRW Inc and Lockheed have won a $1.1 billion Air Force contract to develop an airborne laser system to shoot down ballistic missiles.
- Marvel Entertainment's share fell 41 percent and its bonds plunged after controlling shareholder Perelman announced a $350 million plan to acquire newly issued shares at a steep discount.
- Dell Computer's results were higher than market expectations.
- IBM executives introduced new Internet products.
- Wal-Mart and J.C. Penney results might signal lackluster performance during the holiday season.
- Accountants have tightened rules on detecting fraud in corporate financial statements.
- U.S. Supreme Court rejected a request by the Federal Communications Commission to reinstate rules for opening the local telephone market to competition.
- Japanese officals indicted the chief figure in the Sumitomo copper trading scandal.
- Westinghouse Electric Corp's Jordan will be able to concentrate on the company's broadcasting business after he announces a spin off of its the industrial operations.
- Magellan's Stansky has again boosted his mutual fund's exposure to stocks.

- The U.S. bond market drove the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond lower following a resurgence in the dollar, renewed buzz about a balanced federal budget and expectations that interest rates will stay where they are.
- Questions about HFS Inc's acquisition strategy are arising as it plunders along with its latest purchase of PHH Corp.
-- New York Newsdesk 212 859-1610
